## Which Trips Visit Chiar Khota?

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include [Chiar Khota Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/) on the **main itinerary**. The lagoon's own page describes its natural surroundings in greater detail; here the focus is on selecting a tour whose duration and geography suit you.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_prirodnye_chudesa_bolivii,tour_source_prekrasnaya_patagoniya_i_solonchak_uyuni,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_na_16_dnej_na_novyj_god,tour_south_america_luxury_33_days}}

Current options include the [10-day nature itinerary through Bolivia](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/), [Patagonia and Uyuni in 12 days](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/), an [18-day journey through 5 countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), a [New Year tour through 5 countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) and an [extensive 33-day VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/).

It is the same lagoon, but the context of each trip changes considerably. On the shorter Bolivian itinerary, it is part of an exploration of one country's natural regions. On multi-country journeys, it is one stop among Patagonia's glaciers, capital cities, ancient monuments and salt flats.

## On Which Day Does the Tour Reach Chiar Khota?

| Itinerary | Lagoon Section |
|---|---|
| Bolivia, 10 days | Day 3, chain of lagoons |
| Patagonia and Uyuni, 12 days | Day 10, Uyuni area |
| 5 countries, 18 days | Day 12, transfer toward Uyuni |
| New Year, 5 countries, 19 days | Day 13, Uyuni by 4×4 |
| VIP, 33 days | Day 17, route toward Chile |

On day 3 of the [10-day Bolivia tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/), the road continues from the salt flat toward the Lípez region and the Siloli Desert. Stops include [Cañapa Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/), [Hedionda Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), Chiar Khota and [Honda Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/). Time is allocated for observing nature and taking photographs, with an overnight stay planned in the Siloli area. A private 4×4 vehicle, a bilingual guide and the listed services are provided for that day, but these inclusions should not automatically be attributed to other tours.

On the [12-day Patagonia and Uyuni itinerary](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/), the lagoons are visited on day 10. Chiar Khota appears alongside [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and [Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/) before the journey continues across the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

On the [18-day journey through 5 countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), Chiar Khota is visited on day 12, in a sequence of lagoons before Ollagüe Volcano and the approach to Uyuni. On the [19-day New Year itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/), the comparable section comes on day 13: after the lagoons, the route continues through the Chiguana Salt Flat, Colchani and Incahuasi. The itinerary day matters more than the date embedded in an old filename; check the calendar of your actual departure against the current program.

On the [33-day VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/), Chiar Khota features on day 17, along the route through the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/), the series of lagoons, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), Sol de Mañana and Chalviri toward [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This section is described by the separate [Altiplano lagoons excursion](/bolivia/uyuni/altiplano-lagoons-chalviri-chile-border/).

## Chiar Khota and the Other Lagoons: What Changes Along the Way?

In the Lípez region, high-altitude lakes often follow one another in quick succession. Yet each lagoon has its own appearance. [Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/), [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) and Chiar Khota differ in their shorelines, water colors and surrounding slopes. Flamingos may be seen along some shores, but the number of birds in the wild varies and no particular encounter can be guaranteed.

The lagoon's name is written in several ways, including Chiar Khota, Chiarkhota and Hiar-Khota. These names refer to the same canonical place; different spellings in older itineraries do not indicate different excursions. More important when choosing a tour are the order of stops, the day's duration and whether the route includes Uyuni or continues toward the Chilean border.

Chiar Khota should also be distinguished from [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Red water and large gatherings of flamingos are primarily associated with Colorada. Chiar Khota is worth seeing as one of the smaller lagoons in the chain: its shores and high-altitude views bring variety to the landscape between the salt flat and desert.

## Which Travel Style Is Right for You?

**10 days in Bolivia.** A good choice if you want to explore the Altiplano alongside other natural regions of the country. On the [Bolivia natural highlights tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/), the program moves from Uyuni and Siloli to the Amazonian [Madidi National Park](/bolivia/place/madidi-national-park/) and then to [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/). Chiar Khota is one of the high-altitude days, not the focus of the whole journey.

**12 days including Patagonia.** The [route through Argentina, Chile and Bolivia](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/) connects southern glaciers and mountains with the arid Altiplano. If the contrast between Patagonia and the Uyuni Salt Flat interests you, this option makes more sense than an exclusively Bolivian route. Relatively little of the trip, however, is spent at any one lagoon.

**18–19 days through 5 countries.** The [18-day five-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) and the [19-day New Year option](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) suit travelers who want to combine Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Chiar Khota features during the crossing of the Bolivian Altiplano toward Uyuni. There is also a [19-day “Best Sights of 5 Countries” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) that includes the lagoon on its main route.

**33 days across South America.** The [extensive VIP program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) is designed for travelers ready for a long journey across a wide range of regions. Inclusion in the VIP catalog is no substitute for checking included services: the actual guiding arrangements, accommodation and transport are specified by the itinerary, not by a word in its title.

## Preparing for a Trip to the Altiplano

Days visiting Chiar Khota generally involve driving through high-altitude terrain. Bring warm clothes, protection from sun and wind, shoes suitable for brief lakeside stops, water and an expectation of noticeable temperature changes. Photographing birds requires keeping quiet and maintaining distance, particularly around shallow water.

For those unfamiliar with high-altitude travel, the pace of ascent and acclimatization days are important. Compare not only trip lengths but also the sequence of overnight stops before reaching the Altiplano. If you have health concerns related to altitude, discuss the itinerary with a doctor in advance.

Roads and shorelines usually look different in the dry season than they do after rainfall. Changing weather can affect access to individual stops, and no particular water level, reflection or number of flamingos can be promised for a fixed date. If wildlife observation is your main interest, compare [nature-themed tours of Bolivia](/interests/wildlife/tours/bolivia/).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Chiar Khota Included in the Itinerary or Offered as an Optional Excursion?

For the tours listed in this catalog, it is part of the **main route**. However, the exact stop time, opportunities to walk along the shore and the length of the photography break may differ between programs or may not be specified.

### Is There a Tour That Combines Chiar Khota with Uyuni?

Yes. The [10-day Bolivia tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/), [18-day five-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) and [12-day Patagonia option](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/) combine Chiar Khota with the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), but place them on different days and in different driving sequences.

### Are Flamingo Sightings Guaranteed?

No. Flamingos do inhabit the region's high-altitude lagoons, but their locations and numbers depend on natural conditions. The tour confirms a visit to the lake, not a guaranteed sighting of any particular number of birds.

### How Should I Choose Between the 10-Day and Multi-Country Tours?

If you want to focus on Bolivia and combine the Altiplano with the Amazon and Titicaca, explore the [10-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/). If you also want Patagonia or several countries, compare the [12-day journey](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/) and [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/). The rest of the itinerary, rather than one lakeside stop, should determine your choice.

## Laguna Colorada: Bolivia's Red High-Altitude Lake

**Laguna Colorada** lies in southwestern Bolivia's Potosí Department at approximately **4,278 meters** above sea level. This shallow saline lake is surrounded by dry slopes and the Altiplano's volcanic landscapes. It forms part of the Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve.

The lagoon's defining feature is its **reddish water**, especially striking against the pale mineral shores. Salinity, microorganisms, suspended particles and seasonal water conditions all contribute to its color. NASA and the European Space Agency describe it as a natural feature with changing colors, rather than a surface that remains vivid red at all times.

The name “Red Lagoon” reflects its typical appearance, but the actual tones range from brownish-red to more muted shades; different sections may look different. Visitors should appreciate the entire landscape rather than expect the precise color seen in promotional photographs.

## Why Does the Water Turn Red?

The dry high-altitude climate increases evaporation, while the water accumulates salts. These conditions support microorganisms involved in producing colored pigments. The lake's appearance changes with salinity, temperature, seasonal inflows and light.

Whitish patches along the shore are associated with mineral deposits. The contrast of reddish water, pale edges and brown mountains makes the lagoon recognizable even in images taken from space. Satellite-image colors, however, can depend on which imaging bands were used and may not match what a person sees from the shore.

Do not confuse Laguna Colorada with [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/). Verde is identified with Licancabur Volcano and greenish-turquoise water, while Colorada is known for its shallow depth, red tones and importance to waterbirds.

## Flamingos and Conservation Significance

Laguna Colorada is known for its flamingos. The high-altitude wetlands of southwestern Bolivia are home to Andean flamingos and James's flamingos. These birds use saline lakes to feed, and some parts of the region are particularly important for breeding.

**Flamingos are a natural feature, not a guaranteed tourist attraction.** Their numbers, feeding locations and visibility from any particular stretch of shore vary. Do not approach flocks merely to take photographs: disturbing the birds threatens the colony and conflicts with the purpose of the protected area.

The lagoon and surrounding wetlands are linked to the international Ramsar conservation system. The site was originally listed as a wetland of international importance under the name Laguna Colorada in 1990. The protected area was later extended, and the present Ramsar complex is known as **Los Lípez**. This does not mean that every shore of every regional lagoon is equally open to visitors: access rules depend on the protection zone.

For nature enthusiasts, Laguna Colorada is a worthwhile destination in its own right. Nearby [Chiar Khota Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/) and [Cañapa Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/) offer a chance to compare other high-altitude lakes rather than reduce the whole journey to a single stop.

## Visiting Laguna Colorada on a Route Toward Uyuni

The lagoon is generally reached by off-road vehicle as part of an itinerary through southwestern Bolivia. Saline lakes alternate with desert plateau sections, volcanic scenery and geothermal areas. The onward journey may lead to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), although the order of stops and travel times depend on the entry point and road conditions.

On Ada Tours' current [12-day “Patagonia and the Uyuni Salt Flat” tour](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/), Laguna Colorada is part of the Bolivian high-altitude section alongside Laguna Verde, Chiar Khota and Cañapa. The tour combines Argentina, Chile and Bolivia, so time spent at each lagoon must fit the overall schedule spanning several countries.

Travelers choosing a trip for flamingo sightings should find out how long the stop actually lasts and whether the birds can be observed from a permitted shore. That matters more than how many lagoon names appear in the description. Vehicles and walkers must remain on authorized roads and routes. The reserve has its own rules and checkpoints; check current conditions before departure.

## Altitude and Travel Conditions

The lake lies above 4,200 meters. Thin air, cold mornings, strong winds and intense sunlight make even a short stop noticeably different from an excursion at low altitude.

If you struggle with rapid altitude gain, discuss the itinerary and acclimatization with a doctor beforehand. Headaches, nausea, unusual weakness and breathing difficulties require attention; serious symptoms should never be ignored for the sake of another photo stop.

Carry warm clothing, water, a hat, sunglasses and wind protection in the vehicle. Dust and strong gusts are possible near the shore; comfortable non-slip shoes are more useful than trying to get as close to the water as possible.

## When Is the Best Time to See the Colors and Birds?

There is no single month that guarantees both red water and large flamingo flocks. The color depends on water composition and conditions, while the birds move as feeding conditions change. The rainy season can also affect roads in high-altitude Bolivia.

When planning a visit, think about the wider region: high-altitude lagoons, volcanic deserts and the salt flat. [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) offers a different combination of water color and volcanic scenery, while [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is an entirely different kind of salt-flat landscape.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Laguna Colorada

### Why Is Laguna Colorada Red?

The reddish color is linked to the water's salinity and the activity of microorganisms, including algae, as well as seasonal and lighting conditions. Its shade changes, so the same brilliant color cannot be expected every day.

### Can You See Flamingos Here?

Yes. The lagoon is known for its flamingos and is an important wetland. However, the birds move freely, and sightings depend on the season and where the flock happens to be.

### Where Is Laguna Colorada?

In southwestern Bolivia's Potosí Department, within the Eduardo Avaroa reserve area, at approximately 4,278 meters above sea level.

### Can You Combine Laguna Colorada with Uyuni on One Trip?

Yes. High-altitude road routes can link Laguna Colorada with other Altiplano lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Allow for the altitude, road quality and restrictions within the nature reserve.

## Laguna Colorada: An Optional Day Among Bolivia's Red Lakes

[Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) lies on the high plateau of southwestern Bolivia. Its waters take on reddish and brown shades depending on the light, the lake's condition and microorganisms. Pale mineral shores and flamingos can be seen against the dry slopes. The scenery is very different from the white expanse of the Uyuni Salt Flat.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Laguna Colorada as an **additional stop**. This means travelers on an extended Bolivia journey can choose a separate high-altitude excursion if the itinerary's conditions allow it. Simply mentioning the lagoon does not guarantee an excursion or mean that the transfer is included in the base tour price.

## An Optional Day on the Peru and Bolivia VIP Itinerary

On the [18-day VIP “Machu Picchu, Amazon and Uyuni Salt Flat” tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/), the mandatory Bolivia section covers the Uyuni Salt Flat, stops at Colchani and Incahuasi Island, and accommodation in the salt-flat area. A separate **optional day exploring the Altiplano** is offered, featuring lagoons and flamingo watching.

This additional route includes Laguna Colorada, [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), Cañapa and Chiar Khota, as well as the surroundings of Ollagüe Volcano and the Chiguana Salt Flat. It is a long 4×4 journey through high-altitude terrain; the precise sequence and possibility of visiting every stop depend on roads and the conditions of the particular excursion.

The difference from visiting only the salt flat is considerable: reaching Laguna Colorada means traveling farther into the Lípez region and its high-altitude lagoons. The landscape changes, more time is spent in the vehicle, and the demands of coping with altitude become greater.

## Why Does the Water Turn Red?

The lagoon's color is connected to microorganisms and the conditions of its mineral-rich water, but it changes with light, wind and water level. It would therefore be wrong to promise a consistently vivid red shade like that in an edited photograph. Salt deposits occur on the shores, surrounded by dry high-altitude scenery.

Flamingos are another reason to visit the area. Bolivia's conservation agency SERNAP identifies Laguna Colorada in its protected-area documentation as an important habitat and breeding site for Andean species. It is a place to watch birds, not somewhere to approach them for a photograph.

| What to Compare | Key Detail |
|---|---|
| Red water | Color varies with conditions |
| Flamingos | Wild birds near the shore |

## An Optional Visit or a Tour with Laguna Colorada on the Main Route?

If Laguna Colorada is one of your principal reasons for traveling, consider the [3-day Uyuni and lagoons 4×4 tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). There, the red lake is one of the main stops alongside geothermal areas, volcanoes and the salt flat. It is a different product, with its own duration and included services, and it is not automatically part of the VIP journey through Peru.

On the [15-day Peru and Bolivia tour with Altiplano lakes](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/), high-altitude lagoons are also included in a broader route. These alternatives make it possible to compare how many days are dedicated to southwestern Bolivia versus Cusco, [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and other regions.

## Preparing for Altitude and Birdwatching

Lagoon routes cross high-altitude terrain. Mornings and evenings are cold, the air is dry and solar radiation is intense. Bring a warm jacket, wind protection, sunglasses and plenty of drinking water. The excursion should fit your overall acclimatization schedule, particularly if you have arrived quickly in the Andes.

Road conditions may require a four-wheel-drive vehicle, while stops at the lakes must comply with conservation rules. Do not enter the water, disturb the birds or leave litter. The excursion is an opportunity to observe the natural landscape, not an opportunity for swimming.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Laguna Colorada

### Where Is Laguna Colorada?

In southwestern Bolivia, in the high-altitude Lípez region, within the Eduardo Avaroa protected area.

### Is Laguna Colorada Included in the 18-Day VIP Tour?

It is described as part of an **optional Altiplano day**. The visit requires separate confirmation when choosing the itinerary.

### Are Bright-Red Water and Flamingos Guaranteed?

No. Water color depends on natural factors, and flamingos move freely. They can be observed when conditions are favorable.

### Which Other Lagoons Are Visited with Colorada?

The additional day mentions Cañapa, [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), Chiar Khota and [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), but the actual plan depends on road and weather conditions.

Getting there usually means an off-road drive across desert plains with other natural stops along the way. To choose a trip, compare **where the route starts, which day includes the lake and what follows afterward**. A longer tour does not necessarily mean more hours spent at Colorada.

## From 3 to 33 Days: Comparing the Itineraries

| Tour | When Colorada Is Visited |

| Bolivia, 10 days | Altiplano section |

**[3-day Uyuni 4×4 tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/)** is the most compact of these options. The itinerary starts at the Hito Cajones border crossing and, on its very first day, passes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the [Salvador Dalí Desert](/bolivia/place/salvador-dali-desert/), [Polques Hot Springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) and the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) before reaching Colorada. The overnight stay is in the Eduardo Avaroa reserve area. This tour has specific conditions and exclusions: its description states separately that admission to the reserve must be paid for. Review the [full list of services](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/) when selecting this option, rather than considering only its base price.

**[10-day Bolivia nature tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/)** combines the Uyuni Salt Flat, colorful lagoons and Siloli Desert with a very different part of the country: the Amazonian [Madidi National Park](/bolivia/place/madidi-national-park/) and [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/). This route is well suited to travelers who want to experience Bolivia's natural contrasts and have time for several climate zones.

**[Bolivia in 11 days](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/)** brings together [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), Titicaca, the salt flat, high-altitude lagoons and other parts of the country. Colorada is one stop on a much longer Bolivian journey, rather than the sole purpose of an excursion.

**[Peru and Bolivia: Uyuni and the Altiplano Lakes](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/)** is a 15-day itinerary that visits Colorada on day 11. The same day also includes the Stone Tree in the Siloli Desert, Sol de Mañana geysers, Polques and Laguna Verde. After these natural attractions, a transfer toward Uyuni is planned. This option combines the Peruvian Andes with Bolivia's lakes and salt flat without adding all of Patagonia.

**[Grand South America Tour in 14 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/)** continues through Peru and Bolivia to Chile. On day 11, Colorada is the first major stop, followed by [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), [Chalviri Lake](/bolivia/place/laguna-chalviri/) with an opportunity to bathe in the hot springs, [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) and the transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This is a good choice if you want Peru's cultural sites and the Chilean desert alongside the Bolivian lakes.

**[16-day Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/)** includes Colorada on day 4 en route toward the Chilean border. This section also features [Polques Hot Springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/), Sol de Mañana, [Laguna Blanca](/bolivia/place/laguna-blanca/) and Laguna Verde. The journey then continues across Chile as far as Patagonia. For this kind of trip, the duration of the day's drive and the onward transfer matter as much as the lakes included.

**[Extended 33-day VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/)** visits Colorada on day 17, alongside [Chiar Khota](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/), [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), [Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/), [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), Ramaditas, the geysers and Chalviri. It uses the separate [“Altiplano: Five Lagoons, Colorada and Transfer to Chile” excursion](/bolivia/uyuni/altiplano-lagoons-chalviri-chile-border/). The VIP label does not, by itself, confirm any special facilities on Colorada's shores; the actual services are set out on the tour page.

## Why Is the Water Red, and Will You See Flamingos?

The water's red and burgundy tones are associated with microorganisms and algae living in the saline lake. NASA describes how salinity, temperature and sunlight influence their growth. As a result, **Laguna Colorada does not stay the same color throughout the year**: depending on conditions, the water may appear reddish-brown, brighter red or a noticeably different shade.

The lake is approximately 4,300 meters above sea level. White mineral patches along the shore emphasize the contrast with dark water and dry slopes. The area is open and windy, with sparse vegetation and broad views from the shoreline and nearby roads.

Flamingos can be found at Colorada, including James's flamingos mentioned in some Ada Tours itineraries. The birds feed in the region's shallow saline lakes. However, photographs or general descriptions of the lake do not guarantee that birds will be present in particular numbers at the time of your stop. Maintain a respectful distance and avoid approaching feeding areas.

If birdlife and high-altitude nature are the main focus of your trip, explore [nature tours of Bolivia](/interests/wildlife/tours/bolivia/) and compare how many different lakes and Altiplano days they include. That thematic selection is broader than the catalog of tours specifically passing through Colorada.

## Colorada, Verde and Chiar Khota: Different Roles in an Itinerary

[Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is known above all for reddish water, saline shorelines and flamingos. [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) offers scenery near Licancabur Volcano and water with a different appearance. [Chiar Khota](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/), [Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/) and [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) provide opportunities to compare smaller lakes and bird habitats.

Most 4×4 programs visit several lakes in a sequence, sometimes within a single day. This involves driving between stops rather than walking along the shore from one lagoon to the next. The exact order matters: a route entering from the Chilean border and one departing from Uyuni may cover similar attractions in opposite directions.

Another distinct natural stop is [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), where steam and bubbling mud pools can be seen. It should not be confused with the [Polques bathing pools](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) or the hot springs near [Chalviri](/bolivia/place/laguna-chalviri/). The nature of the thermal stop, whether bathing is possible and which services are included depend on the particular itinerary.

## Choosing a Route Through Laguna Colorada

If you have **3 days** and want to concentrate on western Bolivia, begin with the [4×4 tour of the lagoons and Uyuni](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). Note the starting point: Hito Cajones is a border crossing, so this product should not automatically be treated as a departure from central Uyuni.

With **10–11 days**, compare the [Bolivia nature tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/) and the [Bolivia itinerary with Titicaca and Uyuni](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/). The lagoons are combined with very different regions of the country, so flights, accommodation and changes in altitude across the full itinerary matter.

For **14–16 days**, geography becomes the deciding factor: [Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) or [Bolivia and Chile continuing to Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/). The [12-day Patagonia and Uyuni journey](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/) also visits Colorada, suiting travelers who want to see glaciers in Argentina and Chile as well as the Bolivian Altiplano.

For a long trip with a wide range of experiences, there is the [33-day VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/). If your main interest is the red lake and its neighboring lagoons, compare the shorter trips as well: a longer journey does not necessarily increase the time spent at Colorada.

## Preparing to Visit the High-Altitude Lake

The main practical consideration is altitude. Physical activity feels different on the Altiplano, especially in the first days after arriving from low-lying regions. It is helpful to consider the pace of ascent, rest and hydration, and to discuss the itinerary with a doctor in advance if you have relevant medical conditions. Do not plan a long strenuous walk just because the lake looks close to the road.

Bring warm clothing, protection from wind and sun, and comfortable shoes for stepping out onto the shore. Sunny weather does not necessarily mean warm air. Photographers should prepare their cameras and protect equipment from dust: most visits are short stops along the road rather than extended periods of free time.

Access to individual areas and driving speeds change with weather and the condition of unpaved roads. Itineraries ending in Chile also need time for the border crossing. Without a confirmed schedule, it is impossible to promise an exact arrival time at the lake or a particular number of birds.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tours Through Colorada

### Can You See Laguna Colorada on a 3-Day Trip?

Yes. The [3-day Ada Tours 4×4 itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/) includes Colorada on its first day. Laguna Verde, Polques, Sol de Mañana and the continuing journey to Uyuni are also on the route. Note the specified starting point at the Bolivia–Chile border.

### How Does the Red Lagoon Differ from the Uyuni Salt Flat?

[Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is a relatively small saline lake with reddish water and birds. [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is an immense salt flat known for its white surface in the dry season and mirror-like reflections after rain. They often appear on the same itinerary but offer very different natural experiences.

### Will Flamingos Be Visible in Every Season?

The lake is an important flamingo habitat, but bird numbers and their proximity to viewpoints vary. The itinerary confirms a visit to Colorada, not a particular bird sighting or a photograph taken at a given distance.

### Can You Swim in the Red Lake?

Standard tours treat Colorada as a sightseeing and birdwatching stop. Thermal bathing facilities in the neighboring area are associated with [Polques](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) and [Chalviri](/bolivia/place/laguna-chalviri/), if those visits are part of the itinerary. Do not confuse stopping beside the red lake with bathing in hot water.

### Where Does Eduardo Avaroa Reserve Fit into the Route?

Colorada lies within [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). Admission conditions and the list of included expenses differ between products. On the [3-day 4×4 tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), reserve entry is listed as a separate payment; this condition cannot automatically be applied to every other itinerary.

### Which Tours Combine Colorada and Patagonia?

Current options include [“Patagonia and the Uyuni Salt Flat” for 12 days](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/) and [“Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile” for 16 days](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/). Their duration and the sequence of regions differ, so compare the complete itineraries rather than just the countries listed.

## Laguna Hedionda: A High-Altitude Lake with Flamingos

Laguna Hedionda lies in southwestern [Bolivia](/bolivia/), amid the mountains and high, dry plains of the Lípez region. It is one of the shallow saline lakes of the Andean Plateau. Pale mineral deposits frame its shores, and flamingos can often be seen on the water and in its shallows.

Large mountain ranges on the horizon and wide-open space make Hedionda a striking stop on a road journey. The birds add another dimension: flamingos feed in the water, sometimes gathering in groups, although their numbers and locations depend on the season and natural conditions.

Hedionda is especially interesting as part of a system of high-altitude lakes. Nearby are [Cañapa Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/) and [Honda Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/). Unlike isolated tourist viewpoints, each reveals how water and wildlife endure in the cold, dry and windy highlands.

## Why Is It Called Hedionda?

The Spanish word *hedionda* means “foul-smelling.” The name is associated with an odor that can be noticed near the mineral-rich water and surrounding deposits. The smell, however, varies with the weather and the lake's condition; it is far from the lagoon's only distinguishing feature.

Its ecosystem is even more interesting. The shallow water, with a high concentration of dissolved salts, provides conditions for small aquatic organisms that feed the birds. Saline high-altitude lakes differ from one another in chemical composition, water color and the number of animals living in them.

It is easy to confuse Hedionda with other lakes in southwestern Bolivia, particularly if a description mentions only flamingos and mountain scenery. To distinguish stops on an itinerary, check the actual names: [Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/), Hedionda, [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), [Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and [Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) are separate geographic features.

## Flamingos and Other Birds

Watching Andean flamingos is one of the main reasons to stop at Hedionda. Several flamingo species inhabit Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons. Identifying them at a distance can be difficult, so binoculars or a camera with a telephoto lens are useful.

The birds feed in the shallows. Approaching too closely may cause them to stop feeding or leave the area. Watch instead from permitted points on the shore; avoid walking on damp mineral crusts or attempting to approach the birds for a photograph.

Other high-altitude wildlife may also be encountered in the area, but sightings of any particular species cannot be guaranteed. Treat the lagoon as a natural place where quiet matters, rather than as an organized animal show.

## How Hedionda Fits into Routes Through Uyuni and Lípez

Hedionda is part of the network of road routes through southwestern Bolivia. On Ada Tours journeys, a visit is linked with [Cañapa Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/), [Honda Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) and the continuing route toward the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/). Traveling between these lakes reveals different water colors and how the landscape shifts from mountain slopes to even drier areas.

Trips through the region are often linked to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and routes toward [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). Nevertheless, the location of each lake, the order of stops and the boundaries of protected areas should be distinguished. The general description “Uyuni tour” does not mean the group will visit every lagoon in Lípez.

At Hedionda, a short stop and quiet observation are usually the priorities. Driving may take up most of the time on such itineraries. When choosing a Bolivia trip, compare not only the total length but also the number of substantial stops.

## Altitude, Weather and Safety

The lagoon lies in a high-altitude region more than 4,000 meters above sea level. Even in bright sunshine, cold winds and sharp temperature changes are possible. Bring warm layers, a windproof jacket, sunglasses and water.

Altitude affects how you feel. If the route climbs rapidly from lower elevations, discuss acclimatization in advance and consider individual limitations. Spending an extended period at altitude calls for more careful planning than a brief sightseeing stop in an ordinary city.

This lake is not a beach: saline water, soft bottom sediments and conservation requirements make swimming inappropriate. Stay on accessible paths and follow your guides' advice. Strong winds can raise dust and change photographic conditions within minutes.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Laguna Hedionda

### Where Is Laguna Hedionda?

In southwestern Bolivia, in the high-altitude Lípez region. It is visited on multi-day road journeys through the Andean lagoons.

### Why Are There Flamingos at Hedionda?

The shallow mineral lakes contain organisms that flamingos feed on. The number of birds depends on lake conditions and the season.

### Are Hedionda and Honda the Same Lagoon?

No. Hedionda and [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) are different lagoons. Some itineraries visit them one after another.

### Can You Drive to Hedionda Independently in an Ordinary Car?

Routes cross remote high-altitude terrain where road and weather conditions require careful preparation. For a typical trip, suitable transport and experienced guidance are the safer choice.
